dedupe_keys.name: eelib elenia energy library for prosumer power systems

description: The eELib (elenia Energy Library) is an open Python model library for simulating future power systems with prosumers, households that both consume and produce energy. It is developed by elenia at Technische Universität Braunschweig, was presented at the Open Source Modelling and Simulation of Energy Systems conference in 2024, and has releases up to 1.2.0 on GitLab, with activity into December 2025. It supports building, district and grid scenarios with different shares of distributed devices such as rooftop solar; comparison of energy management strategies such as variable tariffs, multi-use and schedule-based flexibility; the effects of electrified, sector-coupled households on grid limits; economic evaluation of use cases; and market strategies in spot and balancing markets. A Zenodo deposit gives example building and grid scenarios, using a Kerber low-voltage network, with results. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitLab under GPL 3.0 or later at no cost, with documentation on Read the Docs. Caveats: the library targets distribution-level prosumer studies, not transmission. Simulation uses are low-voltage grid impact studies of heat pumps, electric vehicles and solar, and energy management strategy testing. Related records: model-mesmo also models distribution grids with flexible resources.
